description: SM-3 bank-domain metric-suggestion corpus: labelled (table, column) evidence run through the real aida.metric_suggestion_service.score_evidence (SM-4). Every case is a numeric column with an EXACT or SUFFIX MEASURE_KEYWORDS match -- the same gate metric_suggestion_api.generate_metric_suggestions applies before it ever calls score_evidence, so every case here is one the real production pipeline would actually score and could actually propose. ground_truth.correct is a human (steward-level) judgement of whether the proposed (column, suggested_aggregation) pair is actually a valid, correctly-aggregated banking measure -- 14 true positives (plain additive amounts/balances/fees/volumes a human would approve as-is) and 14 false positives (pre-aggregated or cumulative balances, per-unit rates, policy thresholds, and precomputed *_count columns where the keyword-to-aggregation mapping is systematically wrong), chosen for realistic bank-domain ambiguity, not to hit a target score.

cases.business_description: Every card-present and card-not-present transaction. The amount column captures this.

ground_truth.rationale: Plain per-transaction dollar amount; summing across transactions is the standard total-spend metric.

cases.business_description: Cash and check deposits posted to customer accounts.

ground_truth.rationale: Per-deposit dollar amount; summing gives total deposits, a standard banking KPI.

cases.business_description: ATM and teller cash withdrawals. The amount column captures this.

ground_truth.rationale: Per-withdrawal dollar amount; summing gives total withdrawals.

cases.business_description: One row per account per day with its point-in-time balance.
cases.grain_statement: one row per account per snapshot date

ground_truth.rationale: A plain point-in-time balance (no avg/running/closing qualifier); summing across accounts for one snapshot date gives total book balance, a standard metric -- summing across dates would double count, but that is a query-time grouping concern, not a flaw in the base aggregation.

cases.business_description: Outstanding loan balance per loan per day. The balance column captures this.
cases.grain_statement: one row per loan per snapshot date

ground_truth.rationale: Plain outstanding balance per loan; summing across loans for one snapshot date is the standard 'total loan book' metric.

cases.business_description: Every processed card transaction. The fee column captures this.

ground_truth.rationale: Per-transaction fee charged; summing gives total fee revenue, a standard metric.

cases.business_description: Overdraft occurrences and the fee assessed.

ground_truth.rationale: Per-event overdraft fee; summing gives total overdraft fee revenue.

cases.business_description: Loan payment transactions including any late fee assessed.

ground_truth.rationale: Per-payment late fee; summing gives total late fee revenue.

cases.business_description: Interest accrued and recognized per account per period. The revenue column captures this.
cases.grain_statement: one row per account per accrual period

ground_truth.rationale: Per-period interest revenue recognized; summing gives total interest revenue.

cases.business_description: One row per branch per day with same-day deposit totals.
cases.grain_statement: one row per branch per day

ground_truth.rationale: A per-branch-per-day total that is itself additive across branches/days for a coarser rollup (bank-wide daily deposits); this is a legitimate pre-aggregated fact, not a cumulative or averaged one.

cases.business_description: Every processed card transaction. The fee column captures this.

ground_truth.rationale: Per-transaction merchant discount fee; summing gives total merchant fee revenue.

cases.business_description: Confirmed fraud events and the loss amount incurred.
cases.grain_statement: one row per confirmed fraud event

ground_truth.rationale: Per-event confirmed loss amount; summing gives total fraud loss.

cases.business_description: Every processed card transaction with its dollar volume.

ground_truth.rationale: Per-transaction dollar volume; summing gives total processed volume, a standard card-processing metric.

cases.business_description: One row per line item on a customer order.

ground_truth.rationale: Per-line-item unit quantity; summing gives total units ordered.

cases.business_description: One row per account per month with the month's average daily balance.
cases.grain_statement: one row per account per month

ground_truth.rationale: Column already stores a pre-averaged figure; SUMming averages across accounts double-weights nothing meaningful and is not the standard rollup (a weighted AVG is).

cases.business_description: Every posted transaction with the running account balance after posting.

ground_truth.rationale: A cumulative running total already; summing it across transactions is meaningless (compounds an already-cumulative figure).

cases.business_description: One row per account per day with its end-of-day balance. The balance column captures this.
cases.grain_statement: one row per account per day

ground_truth.rationale: An end-of-day snapshot figure; summing across days for one account massively overstates balance (LAST/point-in-time is correct). High evidence (bound term + description mention) does not fix the aggregation being wrong -- this is the calibration-relevant failure case.

cases.business_description: One row per account per day with its start-of-day balance.
cases.grain_statement: one row per account per day

ground_truth.rationale: Same failure mode as closing_balance: a point-in-time snapshot, not an additive measure.

cases.business_description: Reference data describing each product SKU.

ground_truth.rationale: A per-unit rate on a reference table, not a transactional measure; summing per-unit costs across unrelated SKUs has no business meaning.

cases.business_description: Policy configuration per account type/tier.

ground_truth.rationale: A policy threshold configured per account type, not a transactional or snapshot balance; summing thresholds across unrelated tiers is not a meaningful metric.

cases.business_description: One row per customer per day with the day's transaction count. The count column captures this.
cases.grain_statement: one row per customer per day

ground_truth.rationale: Column already holds a pre-computed count per row; the correct rollup is SUM (sum of counts), not COUNT (which would count rows, i.e. customer-days, not transactions). High evidence (bound term + description mention) does not fix this -- the keyword-to-aggregation mapping is wrong for any numeric *_count column.

cases.business_description: One row per customer per month with the month's login count.
cases.grain_statement: one row per customer per month

ground_truth.rationale: Same systematic failure: pre-computed count per row, COUNT(rows) is wrong, SUM(values) is correct.

cases.business_description: One row per branch per day with the day's fraud alert count. The count column captures this.
cases.grain_statement: one row per branch per day

ground_truth.rationale: Same systematic *_count failure, again with high evidence (bound term + description mention) that does not correct it.

cases.business_description: One row per order with the number of line items on it.

ground_truth.rationale: Same systematic *_count failure.

cases.business_description: One row per account per statement period with its ending balance.
cases.grain_statement: one row per account per statement period

ground_truth.rationale: Same failure mode as closing_balance: a point-in-time statement figure, not additive across periods.

cases.business_description: Reference data describing each held security position.

ground_truth.rationale: Already an averaged figure per position; summing weighted averages across unrelated positions is not a meaningful total.

cases.business_description: One row per day with that day's distinct active user count. The count column captures this.

ground_truth.rationale: Doubly wrong: it is a pre-computed distinct-user count (SUM-not-COUNT failure) AND summing daily distinct-user counts across days double-counts returning users, so no single SQL aggregation over this column recovers a correct multi-day total. High evidence (bound term + description mention) does not fix either problem.

cases.business_description: Policy configuration per account type/tier.

ground_truth.rationale: A configured policy ceiling per account type/tier, not a transactional balance; summing ceilings across unrelated tiers is not a meaningful metric.
